entry: Set of rules, norms and standards governing relations among states and other international actors. Also called public international law or the law of nations, it operates largely through [[Consent|consent]], because no universally accepted authority enforces it against [[Sovereign state|sovereign states]]. Its sources are international custom (general state practice accepted as law), [[Treaty|treaties]], and general principles of law recognized by most national legal systems. Violations, particularly of peremptory norms, can draw disapproval or coercive responses, including [[Diplomacy|diplomacy]], economic sanctions and [[War|war]]. The term was coined by [[Jeremy Bentham]] in his 1789 book *Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation*, replacing the older law of nations. Lassa Oppenheim defined it as "a law between sovereign and equal states based on the common consent of these states." Treaties such as the [[Geneva Conventions]] require national law to conform to treaty provisions.

Academic discipline that studies interactions among states and other international actors. Also called international studies or international politics, it is generally classified as a major multidiscipline of [[Political science|political science]] and draws heavily on anthropology, economics, geography, history, law, philosophy and sociology. The most prominent schools of thought within it are realism, liberalism and constructivism. Analysis of international politics dates to antiquity, but the field became a distinct area of study in 1919, when Aberystwyth University in the [[United Kingdom]] first offered it as an undergraduate major. Interest grew after the Second World War, particularly in North America and [[Western Europe]], where the [[Cold War]] shaped the field. The collapse of the [[Soviet Union]] and the rise of [[Globalization]] in the late 20th century prompted new theories and evaluations. Its broader scope includes war, diplomacy, trade, and relations with intergovernmental organizations and multinational corporations.

Exchange of [[Capital (economics)|capital]], goods and services across international borders. Trade occurs because of demand for [[Goods|goods]] or services, and it links local, regional and national economies with the global economy. It moves commodities such as [[Natural resource|natural resources]] and manufactured goods, along with services such as banking, [[Tourism|tourism]], consulting and transportation. A product sold from one country to a party in another is an export from the first and an import to the second. Cross-border trade is typically more costly than domestic trade because of tariffs, non-tariff barriers such as border delays, and differences in language, product safety and legal systems. In 2024, global trade in goods and commercial services reached $32.2 trillion, a 4% expansion from the previous year. Post-World War II institutions, including the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and its successor, the [[World Trade Organization]] (1995), have significantly reduced average tariffs.

American non-profit digital library founded in 1996 by Brewster Kahle. Through archive.org, it provides free access to digitized [[Website|websites]], software, music, audiovisual and print materials, and it advocates a free and open Internet with the mission of "universal access to all knowledge." Its Wayback Machine contains more than 1 trillion web captures, mostly gathered by automated crawlers. The Archive began adding [[BitTorrent]] to its download options in August 2012. In 2023 a federal court ruled that its National Emergency Library and controlled digital lending of scanned books violated publishers' rights; the decision was affirmed on appeal in 2024, and approximately 500,000 titles were removed.

Retired series of graphical [[Web browser|web browsers]] developed by [[Microsoft]] for Windows. First released in 1995 as part of the Plus! add-on package for Windows 95, it was later bundled with Windows, and Microsoft spent over US$100 million per year on it in the late 1990s. Its usage share peaked at 95% by 2003, after bundling helped Microsoft win the first browser war against Netscape. Share declined with the launches of [[Firefox]] (2004) and [[Google Chrome]] (2008). Support ended on June 15, 2022, for [[Windows 10]] Semi-Annual Channel editions. Microsoft Edge succeeded it in 2015, and its core continues as IE Mode until at least 2029.

Network-layer communications protocol in the [[Internet protocol suite]] for relaying datagrams across network boundaries. Its routing function enables internetworking and essentially establishes the [[Internet]]. IP delivers packets from source host to destination host based solely on the [[IP address|IP addresses]] in their headers. Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn introduced it in 1974 as the connectionless datagram service of the original Transmission Control Program. The first major version, [[IPv4]], is the dominant protocol of the Internet; its successor, [[IPv6]], has been increasingly deployed since around 2006.

Cultural item, such as an idea, behavior or style, that spreads across the internet, now mainly through [[Social media|social media]] platforms. The term "meme" was introduced by [[Richard Dawkins]] in his 1976 book *The Selfish Gene* for a conceptual unit of cultural transmission, analogous to a gene. Mike Godwin coined "internet meme" in 1993 for the way memes proliferated through early online communities, including message boards, [[Usenet]] groups and email. The emergence of social media platforms such as [[YouTube]] further diversified memes and accelerated their spread. Internet memes often represent fleeting trends, and their defining traits are creative reproduction, through mimicry or remix, and intertextuality. For example, the phrase "binders full of women" from the 2012 US presidential debate of US politician [[Mitt Romney]] was superimposed on a scene from the Korean pop song "[[Gangnam Style]]". Memes are also the subject of academic research and can raise [[Copyright|copyright]] disputes.

Network of physical objects embedded with [[Sensor|sensors]], processing ability and software that exchange data over the [[Internet]] or other networks. The field draws on embedded systems and [[Machine learning]], and smart home products are the most familiar applications, but the largest are in business and industrial sectors. Commercial asset tracking and fleet management account for 22% of the total market, and trailer and intermodal container tracking reached 5.8 million and 5.3 million active devices globally at the end of 2024. Because connected devices are vulnerable to security breaches and privacy concerns, industry and government have moved to develop standards and regulatory frameworks.

Pornography accessible over the [[Internet]], mainly via [[Website|websites]], FTP connections, peer-to-peer file sharing and Usenet newsgroups. Growth accelerated with the [[World Wide Web]] from the late 1990s. Danni's Hard Drive, started in 1995 by Danni Ashe, is considered one of the earliest such sites. Estimates in 2020 put the number of pornography websites at nearly 30 million, about 12% of all websites. The four most accessed are [[Pornhub]], xHamster, XVideos and XNXX. As of 2025, the company Aylo owns and operates most of the popular streaming sites, including Pornhub and RedTube; some have alleged that it is a [[Monopoly|monopoly]].

Framework organizing the communication protocols used in the [[Internet]] and similar computer networks. Commonly known as TCP/IP, the suite is built on the [[Transmission Control Protocol]] (TCP), the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) and the [[Internet Protocol]] (IP). Its four layers run from lowest to highest: the link layer, for data within a single network segment; the internet layer, for internetworking between independent networks; the transport layer, for host-to-host communication; and the application layer, for process-to-process exchange, which supports protocols such as [[HTTP]]. Its roots lie in research sponsored by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) of the [[United States Department of Defense]] in the late 1960s, which included the [[ARPANET]]. Early versions were called the Department of Defense Internet Architecture Model. The Internet Engineering Task Force maintains its standards, and the suite predates the OSI model.

Wartime policy under which the U.S. government forcibly relocated and incarcerated about 120,000 people of Japanese descent during [[World War II]]. Executive Order 9066, issued by President [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]] on February 19, 1942, followed the [[Attack on Pearl Harbor|attack on Pearl Harbor]]. In 1944 the Supreme Court upheld the exclusion orders in Korematsu v. United States on grounds of military necessity, a decision later repudiated. A commission appointed under President [[Jimmy Carter]] reported in 1983 that internment reflected racism rather than Japanese disloyalty. The Civil Liberties Act of 1988, signed by President [[Ronald Reagan]], officially apologized and authorized a payment of $20,000 to each surviving detainee.

Social association, connection or affiliation between two or more people. Relations vary in intimacy, self-disclosure, duration, reciprocity and power distribution, and they form the basis of [[Social group|social groups]] and societies. Major themes include family, [[Kinship|kinship]], [[Friendship|friendship]], [[Love|love]], [[Marriage|marriage]], business, [[Employment|employment]], clubs, neighborhoods, ethical values, support and [[Solidarity|solidarity]]. Relations may be regulated by law, custom or mutual agreement. Friendships are non-sexual and non-romantic, whereas intimate relationships involve emotional or physical closeness, mutual influence and, for romantic ones, love. Analysis draws on anthropology, communication, economics, linguistics, political science, social work and sociology. In the 1990s the field took shape as relationship science, through the work of Ellen Berscheid and Elaine Hatfield.

Mass and energy that fill the [[Solar System]], through which planets, asteroids and comets move. It ends at the [[Heliosphere|heliopause]], beyond which the [[Interstellar medium]] begins. Before 1950 it was widely considered either an empty [[Vacuum|vacuum]] or filled with "aether." It includes interplanetary dust and gas, [[Cosmic ray|cosmic rays]] and hot [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] from the [[Solar wind|solar wind]], whose density falls in inverse proportion to the square of distance from the Sun. Near Earth the medium contains about 5 particles/cm³, though values as high as 100 particles/cm³ have been observed, compared with about 2.9 × 10¹⁹ particles per cm³ for air at sea level. Its plasma makes the Sun's magnetic field at Earth's orbit over 100 times greater than originally anticipated, at around 7 nT.

International police organization that facilitates worldwide police cooperation and crime control. It is headquartered in [[Lyon]], [[France]], with a National Central Bureau in each of its 196 member states. Founded in [[Vienna]] on September 7, 1923, as the International Criminal Police Commission, it came under Nazi control in 1938, and its headquarters was moved to the Berlin building housing the [[Gestapo]]. It adopted the name Interpol in 1956. Today it focuses on [[Terrorism|terrorism]], cybercrime and [[Organized crime|organized crime]], offering investigative support and training, but it is not itself a law enforcement agency. Its charter bars interventions that are political, military, religious or racial in nature. Critics argue that some member states have used its Red Notices against political dissidents, and reforms include oversight by the Commission for the Control of INTERPOL's Files.

Set containing the elements common to all of some [[Set (mathematics)|sets]]. In [[Set theory|set theory]], the intersection of two sets A and B, written A∩B, is the set of all objects that are members of both. It generalizes to any nonempty collection of sets. For example, {1,2,3}∩{2,3,4} = {2,3}, and {1,2,3}∩{4,5,6} is the [[Empty set|empty set]]. Two sets are disjoint when their intersection is empty. The operation is associative, commutative and idempotent, and it distributes over [[Union (set theory)|union]]. By [[De Morgan's laws]], A∩B equals the complement of the union of the complements of A and B. The concept was generalized from [[Geometry|geometry]], where two distinct non-parallel lines in a plane intersect in a single [[Point (geometry)|point]].

Congenital variation in sex characteristics, such as [[Chromosome|chromosomes]], gonads or genitals, that does not fit typical binary notions of male or female bodies. Sex assignment at birth usually aligns with external genitalia, and births with ambiguous genitals fall in the range of 1:4,500–1:2,000 (0.02%–0.05%). Estimates of the intersex population range from 0.018% (one in 5,500 births) to 1.7%, depending on which conditions are included. Historically, intersex people were called "hermaphrodites" or "congenital eunuchs," terms now considered misleading and stigmatizing. Intersex people face [[Discrimination|discrimination]] from birth or after traits are discovered at puberty. Some infants have been surgically or hormonally altered to create more socially acceptable sex characteristics, a practice considered controversial, with no firm evidence of favorable outcomes. Increasingly, such issues are considered [[Human rights|human rights]] abuses. In April 2015, Malta became the first country to outlaw non-consensual medical interventions to modify sex anatomy.

Nationwide network of [[Controlled-access highway|controlled-access]] freeways in the [[United States]], officially the [[Dwight D. Eisenhower]] National System of Interstate and Defense Highways. Authorized by the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956, signed by Eisenhower on June 29, 1956, it used uniform standards and mostly new routes. Freeway construction displaced one million people in the two decades after 1956. The original system, proclaimed complete in 1992, cost approximately $114 billion. Interstates are owned by the individual [[U.S. state|states]] where they were built. As of 2022, they carried about one quarter of all vehicle miles driven, with more than 5,000 fatalities annually in 2022 and 2023.

Matter and radiation filling the space between the [[Star system|star systems]] in a [[Galaxy|galaxy]]. It includes gas in ionic, atomic and molecular forms, as well as dust and cosmic rays. Within the Milky Way, by mass, about 99% of it is gas and 1% dust, and the gas is about 70% hydrogen, 28% helium and 1.5% heavier elements. It exists in several phases distinguished by temperature and density, and magnetic fields and turbulence provide pressure that is typically more important than thermal pressure. Stars form in its densest regions and return matter through [[Planetary nebula|planetary nebulae]], stellar winds and [[Supernova|supernovae]]. [[Voyager 1]] reached it on August 25, 2012, the first artificial object from Earth to do so, and [[Voyager 2]] entered it on November 5, 2018.

Band of thunderstorms where the northeast and southeast [[Trade winds|trade winds]] converge near the [[Equator]]. Sailors have called it the doldrums for its monotonous, windless weather. It encircles Earth near the thermal equator and shifts seasonally. Its north–south migration largely follows the Sun over oceans, but over continents its position can be decoupled from the region of maximum rainfall. Its convective thunderstorms, driven by solar heating, form the ascending branch of the [[Hadley cell]] and produce a significant portion of global tropical rainfall. Shifts in its position influence the onset and intensity of [[Monsoon|monsoons]] and drought.

[[Interpersonal relationship]] involving emotional or physical closeness, which may include romantic or platonic love and sexual intimacy. Such relationships are interdependent, and their quality depends on the context and history built between partners over time. Formation begins with interpersonal attraction, and researchers find physical attractiveness the largest predictor of initial attraction. Social and legal institutions such as [[Marriage]] acknowledge and uphold intimate relationships, which are not necessarily monogamous or sexual. Healthy relationships benefit psychological and physical well-being, while conflict, external stressors, insecurity and [[Jealousy]] can cause distress and dissolution. The global share of women in a marital or [[Cohabitation|cohabiting]] union fell from 69% in 1970 to around 63% in 2024.

Examination of one's own conscious thoughts and feelings. In [[Psychology|psychology]], it relies on observing one's own mental states and is generally considered to give privileged access to those states, not mediated by other sources of knowledge. Philosophers have discussed it since antiquity; [[Plato]] urged calmly reviewing one's own thoughts. In [[Epistemology|epistemology]], it is compared with perception, reason, memory and testimony as a source of knowledge. [[Wilhelm Wundt]], the father of experimental psychology, used controlled introspection in his laboratory at the University of Leipzig and set strict procedures so that experiments could be replicated. Its use declined with the rise of [[Behaviorism]], championed by [[John B. Watson]], who dismissed it as unverifiable. Modern forms such as think-aloud protocols persist, though researchers recognize its limits, including retrospective bias.

Group of culturally and historically related Indigenous peoples of the [[Arctic]] and Subarctic regions of North America and Russia, whose singular form is Inuk. They have traditionally inhabited [[Greenland]], Labrador, Quebec, [[Nunavut]], the [[Northwest Territories]], Yukon and [[Alaska]]. Inuit languages belong to the [[Eskaleut languages|Eskaleut]] family. The Thule people, ancestors of the Inuit, emerged from the Bering Strait and western Alaska around 1000 CE and spread east across the Arctic, displacing the related Dorset culture. Their use of dogs for transport and larger weapons gave them advantages, and they relied on hunting [[Whale|whales]], seals, caribou and fish. The Inuit population exceeds 150,000, with 70,545 in Canada in the 2021 census. Because many people find the term Eskimo offensive, Inuit is now a common self-designation for a large subgroup of these peoples.

Military offensive by which one polity forcibly enters the territory of another, usually with large numbers of combatants. Its foremost tactical objective is normally to occupy part or all of the invaded territory. Motives have included conquest and annexation, self-defense if the invader was attacked first, liberation, and toppling or altering a government. Today an invasion without prior attack is widely considered an international crime and condemned as [[Aggression|aggression]]. Invasions have been frequent since prehistory, and states with hostile neighbors have built defenses such as rivers, marshes, fortifications and barriers, including the [[Great Wall of China]] and [[Hadrian's Wall]]. Large static defenses became largely obsolete in modern times, as the failure of the Maginot Line at the start of World War II showed. [[Napoleon]]'s 1812 campaign into [[Russia]] illustrates the perils of overextension.

Joint attack on Poland by [[Nazi Germany]], the Slovak Republic and the [[Soviet Union]], which began [[World War II]] on September 1, 1939. German and Slovak forces attacked the morning after the Gleiwitz incident, one week after the [[Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact]] was signed. The Soviet [[Red Army]] invaded eastern Poland on September 17 under a secret protocol dividing the country. The [[United Kingdom]] and [[France]] had declared war on Germany on September 3, but their aid was limited. Germany and the Soviet Union gained full control by October 6, 1939, ending the Second Polish Republic, though Poland never formally surrendered.

Introduced species that harms its new environment, causing ecological, environmental or economic damage. Invasions of established ecosystems occur naturally, but human-facilitated introductions, many through [[International trade|trade]], have greatly increased their rate, scale and range since the [[Age of Discovery]]. Notable invasive plants include [[Kudzu]], [[Pontederia crassipes|water hyacinth]] and common ragweed, while European rabbits, [[Cat|domestic cats]] and red swamp crayfish are notable invasive animals. On [[Guam]], the brown tree snake has extirpated multiple bird taxa after inadvertent importation. Biological invasions are estimated to have cost the United States at least $1.22 trillion in documented damages from 1960 to 2020, and global annual losses exceed $400 billion.
